newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Market yawns on wider spreads.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Market yawns on wider spreads.

text.p: Brazilian debt issuers were expected to steer clear of the primary market this week as investors demonstrate an increasingly poor appetite for the nation's paper.
Only one new issue, a $50 million, five-year bond from investment bank Pactual, was set to be priced this week.

Credit Lyonnais is lead manager for the deal, which was seen pricing at 310 to 330 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. There is some talk that Pactual might raise the issue to $75 million or $100 million.
While it appears the gush of new bank paper has ended, Banco Real said Monday it planned to issue $300 million in Eurobonds by the end of the year.
Director general Rene Aduan said the bonds would carry maturities of three to four years and would be used to finance agriculture and corporate loans.
Banco Real issued a $250 million two-tranche bond in July.
The first tranche was a $175 million three-year bond, which priced at 190 bps over Treasuries. The other, a $75 million four-year bond, came at a spread of 205 bps.

It was still unclear whether Petrobras would meet its goal this week of launching a 30 billion yen ($250 million) six-year bond. Daiwa is leading the well-flagged deal, which was seen pricing at 190-200 bps over Treasuries when swapped into dollars.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, spreads widened by 20 bps on average, traders said.

Brazil's 8.875 percent global due 2001 ZQ4P was one of the poorest performers, widening 25 bps to 180. Brazil 2001 grew even further away from Mexico's 9.75 percent due 2001 ZM5W and Argentina's 9.25 percent due 2001 ZN4D, both of which were trading at a spread of 155 bps, traders said.
Other poor performers included CSN's 9.125 percent due 2007 ZYJJ, which widened 30 bps to 300 over, and Cesp's 9.125 percent due 2004 (put 01), which slipped to 340 over from 320.

Traders said spreads could continue to widen, but one attractive swap was a move out of Petrobras 8.75 percent due 2001 ZPHN, trading at an extremely tight 125 bps over, into Brazil 2001 ZQ4P at 180 bps over.
